summary: Iteration 10 tests the per-account rate-limit fix (phone-only key + X-Forwarded-For for logging). Backend full regression 96/96 pass serially. New iter10 lockout suite 6/7 pass. One HIGH off-by-one bug found in /api/auth/login: the review spec requires attempts 5 & 6 to both return 429, but implementation returns 401 (with empty suffix, left=0) on attempt 5 and only 429 from attempt 6 onward. Per-account bucketing itself works correctly across preview URL / ingress: single doc _id 'phone:<phone>' with count and ip fields, no IP-split buckets. Lockout honors account (correct password during lock -> 429). Change password now clears the correct key. Successful login also clears the counter. Frontend: superadmin login OK, wrong password shows toast 'Nomor HP atau password salah. Sisa 4 percobaan sebelum akun terkunci 15 menit' and user stays on /login. /profile has no 'Failed to fetch'. Billy still shows data-testid=force-password-page. Final state: 1 superadmin, 3 canonical accounts intact, login_attempts empty, .env has no SUPERADMIN_RECOVERY.

critical.issue: Off-by-one lockout: with MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, the 5th consecutive wrong attempt returns 401 with detail 'Nomor HP atau password salah.' (empty 'Sisa' suffix because left=max(0,5-5)=0) instead of 429. Only from attempt 6 onward does _check_lock trigger the 429. Review spec explicitly requires attempts 5 AND 6 to be 429. Fix: either check `count > MAX_ATTEMPTS-1` before incrementing (already done in _check_lock, but semantics need shifting) or, more simply, after incrementing, if new count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS raise 429 immediately with lockout message instead of falling through to the 401 branch. UX also suffers: the 5th attempt tells the user nothing about being locked.

action_items: Backend: fix off-by-one in POST /api/auth/login so attempts 5 & 6 both return 429 (see snippet: after `find_one_and_update`, if `rec['count'] >= MAX_ATTEMPTS` raise 429 with the 15-menit message directly instead of returning 401 with an empty-suffix message).
Optional: after fix, tighten /app/backend/tests/test_iter8_password_change.py TestLoginLockout.test_progressive_messages to strict assertions (Sisa 4/3/2/1 then two 429s) — currently lenient.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_routes.py login(): the branch that increments the counter still returns 401 even when the counter has reached MAX_ATTEMPTS, so the transition into 429 is deferred by one request. Consolidate the lockout check right after incrementing.

auth_routes.py client_ip() uses only the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry without trusting a fixed proxy chain. Fine for logging, but should be documented as untrusted (never use directly as rate-limit key).
change_password uses `lock_key(user.get('phone') or '')` — if phone is falsy the key would be 'phone:' and could delete other empties; safe today but consider a guard.

rca of the issue: Original user bug (superadmin/admin can't login after password change) was fixed in prior iterations. Iteration-9 found that the rate-limit key was 'ip:phone' with request.client.host being the internal proxy pod IP, splitting counters across replicas. Iter10 fix confirmed: `lock_key = phone:<nomor>` and `client_ip` reads X-Forwarded-For only for storage. Verified by hitting the public preview URL (ingress) 6 times and observing exactly one login_attempts doc with `_id='phone:<phone>'` and count>=5 with an `ip` field. Change-password path uses the same key and removes it, so a user who barely locked out and then changes password no longer has a residual lock. Remaining bug: attempt 5 returns 401 instead of 429 because the guard in _check_lock only fires when count>=MAX_ATTEMPTS on the NEXT request; the counter-increment branch never converts to 429 when it just crossed the threshold.
